sentences.text: Heard, learned counsel for the parties.

1. Instant appeal has been filed under Section 30(1)(a) of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 for enhancement of compensation awarded by the learned Presiding Officer, Labour Court, Deoghar in W.C. Case No.43 of 2012.

2. The facts are not in dispute that the deceased workman- Santosh Choudhary was serving as Cleaner in a truck bearing registration no.JH 11G 6195 and died in a motor vehicle accident on 29.07.2012 involving the said truck.

The finding of fact regarding factum of accident is not under Smt. Radhiya Devi Wife Of Rameshwar Gope ... vs Jharkhandi Choudhary Son Of Rameshwar ... on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147890476/
1 challenge from any quarter.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. The claim for enhancement is on the ground that the deceased was aged 23 years and getting salary of Rs.6000/- per month from his employer and he was also being paid Khuraki (Food Allowance) of Rs.100/- per day in addition to that.
4. It is argued by the appellant, and rightly so that Khuraki comes within the definition of wages.

Under Section 2(m) of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, "wages" includes any privilege or benefit which is capable of being estimated in money, other than a travelling allowance or the value of any travelling concession or a contribution paid by the employer of a workman towards any pension or provident fund or a sum paid to a workman to cover 2025:JHHC:11139 any special expenses entailed on him by the nature of his employment.

5. It is further argued that the claimant was entitled to get the interest on the principal amount under Section 4A(3) of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 from the date of accident as simple interest @ 12% per annum.
6. Learned counsel on behalf of Insurance Company defends the impugned order.
It is submitted that the food allowance of Rs.100/- day will not come within the meaning of wages of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923.

7. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the accident took place on 29.07.2012 and on the said date, the amendment to Section 4 of the Workmen's Compensation Act brought on 31.05.2010.

The 2010 amendment, by which the maximum ceiling of wage admissible for computing compensation was Rs.8,000/-
8.

Having considered the submissions advanced on behalf of both the sides and perusing the materials on record, I find merit in the claim for enhancement of the compensation as the food allowance was not added in the monthly income by the learned Tribunal.
Taking Rs.100/- as food allowance and 26 as the working days.
9. In view of the amendment of the year 2010, Rs.8000/- can be taken as the monthly wage of the deceased.

10. The final compensation amount will work out as follows :- Rs.4000/- X 219.95 = Rs.8,79,800/-
(Rupees Eight Lakhs Seventy Nine Thousand Eight Hundred only) along with interest @12% per annum from the date of accident till its realization.
Insurance Company
is directed to make the final payment of the compensation amount within a month of this order.
Misc. Appeal is allowed.
Pending, I.A(s), if any, stands disposed of.

(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Sandeep Smt. Radhiya Devi Wife Of Rameshwar Gope ... vs Jharkhandi Choudhary Son Of Rameshwar ... on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147890476/
